summary: The stash CLI now embeds, at build time, the versions of six release-train packages read from sibling workspace manifests, and uses them to pin every install `stash init` performs, every install hint, the context.json installCommand and the one-shot wizard spawn. It also warns on any exact-version mismatch between node_modules and the embed and, interactively, offers (default yes) to 'align' skewed packages. The fix is well tested for the stale-dist-tag case it targets, and CI (unit, E2E incl. a built-artifact embed check) passed. The main release risk is structural: Changesets versions these packages independently (no fixed group) and stash only dev/optional-peer depends on @cipherstash/stack, so a stack or adapter release does not rebuild stash. The embedded pins then go stale: init installs an older @cipherstash/stack/adapter than is current, and for projects already on the newer version it reports 'skew' and offers to downgrade them, which the shipped stash-cli skill tells agents to accept. That reverses the guarantee the PR claims ('can never disagree with what Changesets publishes') once releases stop moving together, e.g. after GA. A secondary, loud risk is a pin naming a version that was never published. Impact is medium; the downgrade path is untested.

behaviour_changes.description: `stash init` installs @cipherstash/stack, the integration adapter and stash pinned to exact versions embedded at build time instead of bare names resolved via dist-tags.

New version-skew check: any installed release-train package whose node_modules version differs (exact string inequality, newer or older) from the embed is warned about; interactively the same confirm (initialValue true) that installs missing packages also reinstalls skewed packages at the embedded version; non-interactively it only prints align commands.

tsup build reads ../stack, ../stack-drizzle, ../stack-supabase, ../prisma-next, ../wizard and ./package.json and defines __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__ in both bundles; a missing manifest fails the build and a malformed embed throws at CLI module load.

Generated/printed guidance is pinned: missing-package hints, native-binary recovery hint (was stash@latest), install-eql manual note, .cipherstash/context.json installCommand, and `stash wizard` now spawns @cipherstash/wizard@<embedded>.
Shipped skills: stash-cli says installs are pinned and agents must treat a skew warning as a real problem and align; four other skills add a verify-what-resolved note.

failure_scenarios.title: Pins go stale after a sibling release; init installs older packages and offers to downgrade newer ones
failure_scenarios.trigger: @cipherstash/stack (or an adapter, prisma-next, wizard) publishes a new version in a release that does not also bump stash, e.g. a stack patch after GA.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: Versions are captured only when stash is built (tsup.config.ts:33-58). Changesets has no fixed/linked group (.changeset/config.json:5-6) and stash depends on @cipherstash/stack only as a devDependency and an optional peer `>=1.0.0-rc.0` with onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange (packages/cli/package.json:68-78, config.json:12), so a stack release does not bump or rebuild stash; the adapters and wizard have no dependency edge to stash at all. The latest stash therefore keeps pinning the previous versions. versionSkew flags any inequality, including installed > expected (install-deps.ts:74), and interactively folds the 'align' reinstall into the install confirm with initialValue true (install-deps.ts:175-226). The stash-cli skill tells agents to 'treat that warning as a real problem and align versions' (skills/stash-cli/SKILL.md:39).
failure_scenarios.consequence: Fresh `stash init` silently installs an older encryption client/adapter than is current (missing fixes, potentially security fixes) and records it in context.json; projects already on the newer version get a skew warning, and accepting the default prompt or following the skill downgrades @cipherstash/stack/adapters. `stash wizard` runs an older wizard. Recoverable by reinstalling, but it happens through the official setup path and looks intentional.

existing_verification.description: Unit tests cover skew where the installed version is OLDER than the embed (0.19.0 vs fixture) and the align path; CI unit runs passed.

missing_verification: A test where the installed version is newer than the embedded version (should not offer a downgrade, or should default to no).
A release-process check that stash is republished whenever any RELEASE_TRAIN package is published (or that the pins are allowed to lag).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Only treat installed < expected (semver compare) as skew to align, and default the align confirm to false or separate it from the missing-install confirm; soften the skill wording. Release side: put the release-train packages in a Changesets `fixed` group, or pin with a range (e.g. ^embedded) after GA so newer compatible releases are accepted.

failure_scenarios.title: An embedded pin names a version that is not installable from npm
failure_scenarios.trigger: Within `pnpm run build && changeset publish`, stash publishes but a sibling's publish fails or is delayed, or a manifest carries a version that was never published.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The build reads all six manifests before publish (package.json:34; tsup.config.ts:33-58), so the embed is whatever the manifests say, not what reached the registry. Previously a bare name always resolved to something; now an exact spec for a missing version fails the install (install-deps.ts pinned commands) and `stash wizard` fails to spawn.
failure_scenarios.consequence: `stash init` cannot install dependencies for every new user of that stash release until another stash release is published (npm publishes are irreversible). Loud, not silent; users can install manually.

missing_verification: Post-publish smoke check that each embedded name@version resolves on npm before announcing the stash release.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a post-publish step that runs `npm view <pkg>@<version>` for every embedded pin, or publish stash last in the release.

recommended_controls.description: Decide the intended policy for installed > embedded: do not offer a downgrade (semver-compare), and default the align confirm to false or split it from the missing-install confirm. Adjust skills/stash-cli/SKILL.md:39 accordingly.
Add install-deps tests for installed-newer-than-embedded in interactive and non-interactive modes.
Put the RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS packages in a Changesets `fixed` group (or otherwise force a stash release when any of them publishes), or switch to range pins after GA.
After `changeset publish`, verify every embedded name@version resolves on the registry before the release is announced.

evidence.claim: versionSkew flags any installed release-train package whose version !== the embedded version, with no ordering comparison.
Interactive runs add skewed packages to the install commands under one confirm whose initialValue is true.
No fixed or linked groups; updateInternalDependencies patch; onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange true.
stash has no runtime dependency on @cipherstash/stack, the adapters or wizard; only an optional peer >=1.0.0-rc.0 and a workspace devDependency on stack.
Embedded versions are read from sibling workspace manifests at stash build time.
Release train: stash, stack, stack-drizzle, stack-supabase, prisma-next, wizard.
Malformed embed throws at module load; pinnedSpec returns pkg@embeddedVersion or the bare name in source mode.
Shipped skill tells agents to treat a skew warning as a real problem and align versions before continuing.
Skew tests only use installed versions older than the fixture (0.19.0) or unreadable manifests; no installed-newer case.
All 9 check runs on head succeeded, including Run Tests (Node 22, Node 24, Bun), Run E2E Tests and Lint (Biome).
Test checks each train manifest exists with a name and version; nothing checks registry availability.
Release script is `pnpm run build && changeset publish`: all packages built (embed captured) before any publish.
`stash wizard` spawns the runner with @cipherstash/wizard pinned to the embedded version.
context.json installCommand uses the pinned @cipherstash/stack spec.
PR states the embed 'can never disagree with what Changesets publishes together', which only holds for packages published in the same release as stash.
Repository is in Changesets pre-release mode with tag rc.
